articles.title: MirraArena Multiplayer VR Averages 1,500+ Sessions Per Month Across China FEC Locations
articles.summary: MirraArena's multiplayer VR platform has logged over 1,500 game sessions and nearly 5,000 arena entries per location per month across four China FEC venues, demonstrating strong commercial performance for location-based VR. The data provides compelling proof-of-concept for FEC operators considering adding multiplayer VR as a high-throughput attraction. The results suggest branded, social VR experiences can drive repeat visitation and significant per-venue revenue.

articles.title: Zero Latency VR Sets December 2026 Launch for Jumanji: The Lost Levels, Targets Family Market
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR will launch Jumanji: The Lost Levels on December 4, 2026, developed with Sony Pictures and available at locations worldwide. New survey data shows 60% of visitors now come with family members and the largest demographic is adults 35-44, signaling a major shift in LBE VR's audience. FEC operators with VR attractions should take note of this family-first positioning and the demand for IP-driven experiences.

articles.title: Zero Latency VR Releases Family Audience Data Ahead of Jumanji Launch
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR's new consumer research across five countries shows 92.8% of respondents are interested in VR experiences, and families now represent the dominant visitor group at location-based VR venues. The Jumanji: The Lost Levels experience launches December 4, 2026, and is Zero Latency's first fully hand-tracked title, removing the barrier of controller hardware. FEC operators should use this data to rethink VR marketing strategies and age-appropriate programming.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Intensifies $13.3 Billion Indoor Entertainment Center Buildout
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is accelerating a massive $13.3 billion investment in indoor entertainment centers as part of its Vision 2030 leisure diversification strategy, creating enormous opportunities for international FEC suppliers and operators. The scale of development rivals any regional market globally and is drawing attention from attractions, technology, and design companies worldwide. FEC industry stakeholders should monitor procurement pipelines and partnership opportunities emerging from this buildout.

articles.title: Semnox and Uplay Complete Six Venue Management Projects Across Benelux in First Year
articles.summary: Semnox Solutions and Dutch-Belgian amusement operator Uplay have completed six venue management and cashless technology installations across the Netherlands and Belgium in their first year of partnership. The collaboration demonstrates how technology providers and regional amusement operators can scale modern guest experience infrastructure efficiently. FEC operators in Europe and beyond can look to this model as a template for upgrading payment and operations systems.

articles.title: Semnox and Uplay Mark One Year of Benelux Partnership With Six Completed FEC Projects
articles.summary: Semnox Solutions and Uplay are celebrating the completion of six venue management projects across the Benelux region and will showcase their work at IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 in London this September. The partnership highlights how cashless technology and integrated venue management platforms are becoming standard infrastructure for European FEC operators. Operators attending IAAPA Expo Europe can see the results firsthand and evaluate similar solutions for their own venues.

articles.title: Family Entertainment Group Reaches 100-Location Milestone, Partners With Margaritaville at Sea
articles.summary: Family Entertainment Group LLC has celebrated its 100th location milestone with a landmark partnership aboard Margaritaville at Sea, expanding FEC concepts into the cruise sector. The milestone underscores the scalability of family entertainment franchises and the growing appetite for FEC-style programming in non-traditional venues. Operators and investors should note how leading FEC brands are leveraging partnerships to access new guest demographics.

articles.title: XBOX and BBC Studios to Address LBE and IP Licensing at Brand Licensing Europe 2026
articles.summary: XBOX and BBC Studios will present sessions at Brand Licensing Europe 2026 focused on franchise building and the rapidly growing location-based entertainment market, taking place October 6-8 in London. For FEC operators and attraction developers, this signals that major IP holders are increasingly treating LBE as a strategic licensing channel rather than an afterthought. Operators considering IP-driven attractions should follow the insights shared at this event closely.

articles.title: Social Gaming Venue Time Mission to Open Downtown Boston Location in Early 2027
articles.summary: Time Mission, a social gaming venue concept, has announced a downtown Boston location with construction beginning later this year and an opening planned for early 2027. The expansion of social gaming concepts into major urban markets reflects continued consumer demand for interactive, group-oriented entertainment experiences. Traditional FEC operators should monitor social gaming venue growth as both competition and potential model for urban format development.

articles.title: Adventure Landing Raleigh Closes Abruptly After 38 Years of Operation
articles.summary: Adventure Landing in Raleigh, North Carolina, has suddenly shut its doors after 38 years, ending one of the region's longest-running FEC operations. The abrupt closure highlights the ongoing challenges facing legacy FEC venues that have not modernized their attraction mix or guest experience in line with evolving consumer expectations. This serves as a cautionary tale for operators about the importance of continuous reinvestment and relevance.

articles.title: Raleigh's Adventure Landing Shuts Down After 38 Years
articles.summary: Adventure Landing, a long-established FEC and entertainment destination in Raleigh, has closed abruptly after nearly four decades in business. The sudden closure raises questions about the viability of traditional FEC models that have not kept pace with the experiential entertainment market. Industry observers and operators should examine what factors led to the closure as a lesson in long-term venue sustainability.

articles.title: Minnesota Bowling Centers Reinvent Themselves to Stay Competitive
articles.summary: A new report examines how Minnesota's bowling businesses are evolving beyond traditional lanes by adding food and beverage upgrades, arcade attractions, and event programming to remain relevant. The trend mirrors a national shift in bowling center operations toward full-service FEC models. Operators in the bowling segment can draw directly applicable lessons from these Minnesota case studies.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Signs Lease for First Montana Location
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment has signed a lease for its first Montana venue, continuing the trampoline park and FEC chain's geographic expansion into new markets. The move signals growing confidence in the viability of large-format family entertainment in smaller regional markets. Operators and investors tracking the trampoline park sector should note Launch's continued growth trajectory.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Converting Former Dillard's Department Store in Denton, Texas Into FEC
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is transforming a vacant Dillard's department store in Denton, Texas into a large-format family entertainment center, with an opening planned for this fall. The project is a strong example of adaptive reuse of retail real estate, a growing trend providing FEC operators with affordable large footprints in high-traffic shopping centers. This model continues to gain traction as anchor retail vacancies persist nationwide.

articles.title: India's Imagicaaworld Pivots to Indoor Entertainment With 4-5 New Hello Park Launches Planned Annually
articles.summary: Indian entertainment company Imagicaaworld is expanding aggressively into indoor FEC-style venues through its Hello Park brand, targeting four to five new location launches per year. The strategy reflects growing demand for indoor family entertainment in India's rapidly urbanizing middle-class market. International FEC suppliers and franchisors should view this as a significant emerging market opportunity.

articles.title: SEVEN Opens New Indoor Entertainment Hub in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: SEVEN, the Saudi entertainment giant, has opened a new indoor entertainment destination in Tabuk, adding to its rapidly expanding portfolio of venues across the kingdom. The opening is part of Saudi Arabia's broader multi-billion dollar push to build a domestic leisure economy under Vision 2030. FEC suppliers and operators should pay close attention to SEVEN's venue format and attraction mix as the company scales.

articles.title: SEVEN Tabuk Opens With Cyber Bowling, Indoor Golf, and More Entertainment Options
articles.summary: SEVEN's new Tabuk venue features cyber bowling, indoor golf, and a broad range of entertainment attractions, opening just days after the debut of SEVEN Abha. The rapid multi-city rollout demonstrates how Saudi Arabia's SEVEN is becoming one of the most aggressive FEC operators in the world. Bowling and indoor golf suppliers in particular should note the scale of demand this operator represents.

articles.title: TrainerTainment's Genevieve Sullivan to Present Staff Training Session at Amusement 360
articles.summary: TrainerTainment will deliver a session titled Build it Once: Designing Staff Training That Sticks at Amusement 360 on August 26, aimed at FEC operators looking to create more durable employee training programs. Effective staff training is one of the most critical operational challenges for FEC venues, directly impacting guest experience and retention. Operators attending Amusement 360 should prioritize this session for actionable workforce development strategies.

articles.title: IATP Partners With TheHopeLine to Support Young FEC Employees and Guests
articles.summary: The International Adventure and Trampoline Parks Association has partnered with TheHopeLine, a free 24-hour crisis chat service, to provide mental health support resources for young employees and guests at member venues. As FEC venues frequently employ teenagers and serve youth demographics, having mental health resources available is both a community responsibility and a risk management consideration. Trampoline park operators and other IATP members should integrate awareness of this resource into staff onboarding.

articles.title: Guy Fieri's Downtown Flavortown FEC Opens at Myrtle Beach Mall
articles.summary: FACE Amusement Group and Guy Fieri are holding the official ribbon cutting for Downtown Flavortown Myrtle Beach on September 10, 2026, at Myrtle Beach Mall, combining celebrity IP with an amusement center concept. The project is a high-profile example of celebrity and food IP being layered onto a traditional FEC format to differentiate the guest experience. FEC developers and operators should track how this celebrity-branded model performs in the competitive Myrtle Beach entertainment market.

articles.title: Mr. Gatti's Pizza Targets Lubbock Return With New Family Entertainment Center Concept
articles.summary: Mr. Gatti's Pizza is seeking a franchisee to bring its pizza-plus-FEC concept back to Lubbock, Texas, reflecting the brand's continued push to grow through franchise development. The pizza-and-play model remains a resilient FEC format, and Mr. Gatti's expansion efforts signal renewed confidence in the category. Prospective franchisees and operators in secondary markets should evaluate this opportunity as the brand seeks regional growth.

articles.title: Africa Emerges as Amusement Industry's Next Frontier
articles.summary: A new market report identifies Africa as an emerging opportunity for the amusement and attractions industry, with growing middle-class populations and increasing demand for family entertainment across multiple countries. The report positions Africa as one of the least-penetrated major markets globally for FEC and amusement concepts. Operators, investors, and suppliers with an appetite for high-growth emerging markets should study this analysis closely.

articles.title: Bergen County Entertainment Center Liquidating Trampolines, Bowling Lanes, and VR Equipment at Auction
articles.summary: A major entertainment center in Bergen County, New Jersey is auctioning off its full suite of attractions including trampolines, bowling lanes, and a virtual reality arena. The auction represents both a cautionary signal about venue viability and a buying opportunity for operators looking to acquire FEC equipment at below-market prices. Operators planning new builds or expansions should monitor this sale for cost-effective equipment sourcing.

articles.title: Fantasy Island Entertainment Center Breaks Ground at Former Ship Bottom CVS Site
articles.summary: Construction has begun on a new Fantasy Island Entertainment Center in Ship Bottom, New Jersey, converting a former CVS pharmacy into a family entertainment destination. The project is another example of adaptive retail reuse gaining popularity in the FEC sector as vacant storefronts offer accessible real estate in established communities. Local FEC development activity in the Northeast signals continued consumer demand for indoor family entertainment options.

articles.title: 9D Simulator Cinema Hubs Positioned as Foot Traffic Drivers for Arcade Operators
articles.summary: A new industry analysis highlights how 9D motion simulator cinema attractions can serve as anchor experiences within arcade venues, drawing incremental foot traffic and generating high per-play revenue. The format offers a relatively compact footprint with premium pricing potential, making it attractive for FEC operators looking to differentiate their arcade floor. Operators evaluating new attraction categories should consider simulator-based experiences as a complement to traditional redemption and gaming.

articles.title: Monster Mini Golf Opens New Grimes, Iowa Location
articles.summary: Monster Mini Golf has opened a new franchise location in Grimes, Iowa, continuing the blacklight mini golf chain's steady national expansion. The opening reflects sustained franchisee interest in the indoor mini golf format, which has proven durable across a range of markets. Prospective FEC franchisees and investors tracking the indoor mini golf category should note Monster Mini Golf's growth momentum.

articles.title: Six Flags Expands Fright Fest With 29 New Licensed Haunted Attractions Across Its Portfolio for 2026
articles.summary: Six Flags is rolling out 29 new and returning licensed haunted attractions across its park portfolio for the 2026 Halloween season, including 196 themed scare zones and live entertainment. The scale of IP licensing for seasonal events demonstrates the growing commercial importance of franchise partnerships in driving attendance during the Halloween period. Smaller FEC operators running haunted attractions should take note of the IP licensing strategies being deployed at the park level.

articles.title: Dry Slide Indoor Park Coming to Massachusetts as Retail Conversion
articles.summary: A new dry slide park concept is set to open in Massachusetts as part of a wave of indoor entertainment venues converting vacant retail space across the region. Dry slide attractions represent an emerging format that operators can deploy in relatively modest footprints with lower capital costs than traditional trampoline or water park buildouts. FEC operators and developers exploring new attraction formats should monitor this concept's performance in the Northeast market.
